answer: Dynamic memory-bus contention graphs neutralize automated clones. Candidates execute serialized, cache-thrashing pointer jumps over a 16GB non-compressible ring buffer, recording round-trip timing deviations on a local verifiable log. A designated authority issues a secret challenge seed like a signing quill, forcing nodes to commit state snapshots to a broadcast tree. Generating the valid cryptographic pearl requires dedicated memory channels; spoofing 10,000 parallel identities demands 160TB of high-bandwidth RAM costing $480,000, diverting data like a diverted river.
